findings.summary: the corpus's expect_ids use the symbolic forms ('*', '*AND*', '*both*') rather than concrete material ids — the honest reason: the suite's fixture seeds uuids at runtime (the fresh scratch DB), so the corpus cannot carry them statically; the evaluator compares against the run's own admissions (the deterministic shape)
the evaluator's per-case verdict counts ids, not id equality (the same runtime-seeded-uuid reason); the conflated + distractor + no-result classes ARE id-exact in the suite's own pins
the eval-runs.jsonl append grows across suite runs (the scratch DB drops; the JSONL persists in the slice runs — bounded by the repository's own history discipline)

the suite imports harness.adapters.pg for the scratch DB (the SAME standing dependency every retrieval suite uses — the legal 'from harness.adapters import pg' form adopted; eval.py itself imports only the standard library + subprocess to the standing query arm)

the hostile-as-data marker is a presence count, not a behavioral differential (the stronger form — a probe comparing the run's verdict with/without the hostile case — routed to the D-042 review's own probes)
